ingredientSections.heading: Brine
items: 3 or more Cloves Garlic, partially crushed

ingredientSections.heading: Dredge Mix
items: 1 Tbsp Granulated Garlic or Onion or both
1 Tbsp Dried Thyme or Oregano or both

ingredientSections.heading: Collard Greens
items: 2 small Red or Walla Walla Onions, chopped finely
½ to 1 Bulb Garlic, peeled, in slivers
1 Tbsp Apple Cider Vinegar or Lemon Juice

ingredientSections.heading: Maryland Cream Gravy with Bacon
items: The leaves of 4 or 5 Thyme Stems
Chives or Green Onions to garnish

methodSections.heading: Fried Chicken
steps: Using a boning knife, section the chicken into pieces or have your butcher do it. Halve or quarter the breasts.
Place the chicken in a large container with all the brining ingredients and stir to combine. Use enough buttermilk to submerge all of the chicken. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
In a shallow bowl or casserole dish mix the dredge ingredients together.
Remove the chicken from the fridge, pour off some of the brine into a large bowl and beat in the egg.

One at a time, dredge each piece of chicken in the dredge mix ensuring it is evenly coated on all sides, shake free any excess, dip in buttermilk-egg bath and then back in the dredge mix again. Shake free any excess again and place on a wire rack over a tray.
Repeat with all the chicken. The dredge will start to get shaggy for the last bits. Press the shaggy bits into crevices for extra crispy crust. Let rest for 10 minutes to allow dredge to adhere.

Melt the lard (or Crisco) in a large cast iron Dutch oven or pot on the stove top. The lard/oil needs to be roughly 10cm (3-4in) deep, top up with vegetable oil if necessary. Heat the lard/oil to 180°C (350F).

Cook around four pieces of chicken in the lard/oil at a time. The oil temp will fall to about 150°C (300°F) when the chicken goes in and then climb again as the chicken cooks. The ideal frying temperature is 160-180°C (325- 350°F), monitor this and adjust heat as necessary. Too low and chicken skin will go white and never turn golden. Too high and the skin will burn before the chicken can cook to the bone.

Turn the chicken once or twice, allow roughly 10-12 minutes per side depending on the size or until it is golden brown and reaches an internal temperature of 85°C (180°F). Remove from oil, drain on a wire rack.
If the chicken is starting to burn before it is cooked on the inside bake it in the oven at 190°C (375°F) until it reaches the internal temperature.

methodSections.heading: Collard Greens
steps: Wash, strip leaves from stems and coarsely tear or chop the collards. In a large pot sauté the onions in oil until golden. Add the chilies and garlic and cook until the garlic starts to soften.
Add collards, stock and some liberal shakes of salt. Bring to a boil and then simmer and reduce for at least 40 minutes.
About 10 minutes prior to serving stir in about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar or lemon to brighten and sprinkle with smoked salt to taste.

methodSections.heading: Layered Biscuits
steps: Preheat the oven to 210°C (415°F). Sift the dry ingredients together in large bowl. Grate the butter into the flour. Work the butter into the flour pinching it together with your fingers. It should be in consistently sized small clumps, well coated and evenly distributed. Don't over-work, the butter needs to stay as cold as possible.

Make a well in centre of the flour and pour in the buttermilk. Stir rapidly around the edges of bowl with a wooden spoon until the dough barely comes together. Turn out onto floured work surface. Gather the dough together with hands, do not knead, and gently roll it out into an rectangle about 2cm (¾in) thick .

Fold the dough rectangle like you would fold a letter to put in an envelope. Fold the top down part way and then the bottom up over the top so the rectangle is folded in thirds. Gently roll out again, repeat two more times and then roll out a final time. Handle lightly, overworked dough makes tough biscuits.

Cut out with a biscuit cutter or make rectangular biscuits with a knife. Scraps can be gathered together to cut out more biscuits but do this only once, repeated handling of final scraps doesn't make for good biscuits. Do not twist the cutter or rock the knife, this would seal the edges of the biscuits and prevent them from rising.
Place on a baking tray about ½ inch apart and bake until puffed and golden, 9-15 minutes.

methodSections.heading: Maryland Cream Gravy with Bacon
steps: Fry the bacon in a fry pan and when crispy remove from the pan, set aside, and leave the drippings behind. Sprinkle the flour over bubbling bacon fat and stir well making a blond roux.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until the aromas are toasty.
Add the cayenne, thyme, black pepper, chicken stock and milk or cream. Cook and reduce slightly until it thickens. Chop up the cooked bacon and return it to the pan.
If gravy is too thick add more milk, stock or a few pats of butter. Cream gravies need salt, season to taste.
Garnish with fresh finely cut chives or green onion.
